summary:
1. ultralytics 8.4.218 (PyPI, 2026-11-23, AGPL-3.0, requires Python >=3.8; use 3.12) with torch 2.15.0 / torchvision 0.29.2. NumPy 2 is supported (on macOS 2.0-2.3.4 are excluded). It depends on opencv-python (non-headless).
2. Newest released line is YOLO26 (n/s/m/l/x; -seg trained on COCO-80, -obb on DOTAv1-15). YOLO27 is documented as a preview only: no weights, no code. No pretrained class matches a small coloured cube (COCO, DOTAv1, Objects365 checked), so closed-set YOLO needs fine-tuning.
3. Best fit once labels exist: fine-tuned yolo26n/s-obb (centre, angle and 4 corners directly) or yolo26n/s-seg plus cv2.minAreaRect. Weights are 6-24 MB.
4. Label-free options that fit the disk: YOLOE-26 seg (text prompt, visual prompt, prompt-free) and FastSAM-s (segment everything, 24 MB, 58 ms/img on an M4 CPU). Take colour from HSV on the mask, not from the model.
5. Text prompts cost extra disk: a git-installed clip package plus mobileclip2_b.ts 254 MB (YOLOE-26), mobileclip_blt.ts 600 MB (YOLOE-11/v8), CLIP ViT-B-32.pt 354 MB (YOLO-World), clip_b32_datacomp.ts 303 MB (FastSAM texts).
6. SAM wrappers: MobileSAM (41 MB) and SAM 2.1 t/s (78/92 MB) suit box/click prompts and auto-labelling; "segment everything" took 23-42 s per image on an M4 CPU. SAM 3 is manually gated on Hugging Face and 3.45 GB: skip.
7. M4 figures from primary sources: YOLO26n at 640 is about 18.5 ms wall per image on MPS (MacBook Air M4); on CPU PyTorch n/s/m take 25.6/60/137 ms; CoreML FP16 takes 6-14 ms. Nothing is published for imgsz 1280.
8. On a Mac an unset device means CPU: pass device="mps". Results.speed is not synchronised on MPS, so measure wall-clock time in the app.
9. YOLO26 predict now defaults to the NMS head; nms=False selects the NMS-free head. half= is deprecated in favour of quantize=16.
10. Bare weight names download into the current working directory: pass absolute paths. Set YOLO_CONFIG_DIR and YOLO_AUTOINSTALL=False, and settings sync=False.
11. Zero-shot segmenters mask the whole visible cube, side faces included (about 27 px of side face at the image edge by my geometry estimate), which biases centre and angle. Top-face labels on a fine-tuned model avoid this.

candidates.what: Rotated-box detector. One forward pass gives class, centre, w, h, rotation and the 4 corners per cube, which is exactly the required output. The pretrained checkpoints are DOTAv1 aerial models (plane, ship, storage tank, ... 15 classes), so they only serve as an initialisation. Use: fine-tune on 4 classes (R/G/B/wood) with top-face corner labels (label line: class x1 y1 x2 y2 x3 y3 x4 y4, normalised), then load best.pt in the lab through the upload path. YOLO26 adds an angle loss aimed at square objects. Weights: yolo26n-obb.pt 5.9 MB, yolo26s-obb.pt 21.7 MB, yolo26m-obb.pt 48.4 MB.
candidates.fit_for_task: Best match to the output spec if a labelled set can be made before the competition (probably 50-150 overhead frames; SAM or FastSAM can speed up labelling). Without fine-tuning it is useless on cubes. Rotation is defined modulo 180 degrees and xywhr is not canonicalised, so reduce to modulo 90 for a square and take corners from obb.xyxyxyxy. Colour as a class should be easy for a trained model, but lighting shifts argue for varied training frames.
candidates.weights_id: yolo26n-obb.pt (also yolo26s-obb.pt, yolo26m-obb.pt) from github.com/ultralytics/assets release v8.4.0
candidates.licence: AGPL-3.0 (code and Ultralytics weights; Enterprise licence otherwise)
candidates.mps: works with device="mps" (must be passed explicitly). Rotated NMS is pure torch (TorchNMS.fast_nms with probiou). An older MPS box-clamp bug was fixed in 8.4.111. Fine-tuning on MPS is supported; several MPS training memory fixes landed in 2026.
candidates.latency_note: No published M4 number for OBB. Reference points: YOLO26n detect at 640 on a MacBook Air M4 with MPS = 11.9 ms inference, 18.5 ms wall per image (PR #26850); CPU PyTorch 640x640 = 25.6 ms (n), 60.0 ms (s), 137.2 ms (m). My estimate for 1280x720 frames at imgsz=1280 (letterboxed to 1280x736, about 2.3x the pixels): roughly 30-50 ms for n and 60-100 ms for s on MPS. Not measured.
candidates.ram_note: Estimate, not measured: under 1 GB process memory for n/s models including torch.
candidates.snippet:
from ultralytics import YOLO
import numpy as np

model = YOLO("/abs/project/weights/best-obb.pt")  # fine-tuned; pretrained yolo26n-obb.pt is DOTAv1 only
print(model.task, model.names)  # 'obb', {0: 'red', 1: 'green', ...}
r = model.predict(frame_bgr, device="mps", imgsz=1280, conf=0.25, verbose=False)[0]
if r.obb is not None and len(r.obb):
    xywhr = r.obb.xywhr.cpu().numpy()        # (N,5) cx, cy, w, h, rotation [rad], not canonicalised
    corners = r.obb.xyxyxyxy.cpu().numpy()   # (N,4,2) pixel corners
    cls_ids = r.obb.cls.int().tolist()
    confs = r.obb.conf.tolist()
    angle_mod90 = np.degrees(xywhr[:, 4]) % 90
print(r.speed)        # {'preprocess': ms, 'inference': ms, 'postprocess': ms}
overlay = r.plot()    # annotated BGR ndarray

# fine-tune (dataset yaml with OBB labels):
# YOLO("/abs/project/weights/yolo26n-obb.pt").train(data="cubes-obb.yaml", imgsz=1280, epochs=100, batch=8, device="mps")

candidates.family: Ultralytics YOLO26 instance segmentation (closed-set, fine-tuned or uploaded .pt)
candidates.what: Instance segmentation: boxes plus per-instance masks and polygons (masks.xy). For cubes: fine-tune on 4 classes with top-face polygons, then cv2.minAreaRect on each polygon gives centre, angle and 4 corners. The pretrained yolo26*-seg.pt are COCO-80 models; coco.yaml has no cube or block class. This candidate is also the generic "upload your .pt" path: YOLO(path) reads task and class names from the checkpoint and auto-routes YOLOE, YOLO-World and RT-DETR checkpoints. Weights: yolo26n-seg.pt 6.7 MB, yolo26s-seg.pt 23.5 MB, yolo26m-seg.pt 54.8 MB. Objects365-pretrained variants (yolo26n-objv1-seg.pt 7.2 MB) exist as an alternative starting point; Objects365 has no cube class either.
candidates.fit_for_task: Strong once fine-tuned; pretrained COCO weights will not find the cubes. Versus OBB: the mask boundary gives corners indirectly and is coarser. Masks are produced at reduced resolution unless retina_masks=True, so for 61 px cubes run imgsz=1280 with retina_masks=True. It tolerates partial occlusion by the arm better than a rigid box. Include the pretrained n/s weights as the default loadable baseline and the fine-tune target.
candidates.mps: works with device="mps". torchvision has a native MPS NMS kernel, so the default NMS head needs no CPU fallback. nms=False selects the NMS-free one-to-one head (at most 300 detections, no NMS). FP16 is requested with quantize=16 (half= is deprecated); its effect on MPS is untested here.
candidates.latency_note: Official on an M4 Air CPU: YOLO26n-seg ONNX 25.2 ms per image. Seg FLOPs are about 1.7x the detect model (9.3 B vs 5.5 B for n). My estimate on MPS for 1280x720 frames: n about 15-25 ms at imgsz=640 and 40-70 ms at imgsz=1280 with retina masks; s about 2x. Not measured.
candidates.ram_note: Estimate: under 1 GB for n/s; retina masks at 1280x720 with a dozen cubes are negligible.
candidates.snippet:
from ultralytics import YOLO
import cv2, numpy as np

model = YOLO("/abs/project/weights/yolo26n-seg.pt")  # absolute path: downloaded there if missing; or an uploaded best.pt
meta = {"task": model.task, "names": model.names,                       # e.g. 'segment', {0: 'person', ...}
        "arch": (getattr(model.model, "yaml", None) or {}).get("yaml_file"),
        "train_imgsz": (model.ckpt or {}).get("train_args", {}).get("imgsz")}
r = model.predict(frame_bgr, device="mps", imgsz=1280, conf=0.25, retina_masks=True, verbose=False)[0]
cubes = []
if r.masks is not None:
    for poly, box in zip(r.masks.xy, r.boxes):          # poly: (P,2) float32 pixel polygon
        if len(poly) < 3:
            continue
        rect = cv2.minAreaRect(poly.astype(np.float32))  # ((cx, cy), (w, h), angle_deg)
        cubes.append({"cls": r.names[int(box.cls)], "conf": float(box.conf), "center": rect[0],
                      "angle_mod90": rect[2] % 90, "corners": cv2.boxPoints(rect).tolist()})
print(r.speed)   # per-stage ms; on MPS measure wall-clock yourself
overlay = r.plot()
# video: for r in model.predict("clip.mp4", stream=True, device="mps", imgsz=1280): ...

candidates.family: Ultralytics YOLOE-26 open-vocabulary segmentation, text prompt
candidates.what: Open-vocabulary detector and segmenter: class names are given as strings at inference and every detection carries a mask. Generations shipped: yoloe-26{n,s,m,l,x}-seg.pt, yoloe-11{s,m,l}-seg.pt, yoloe-v8{s,m,l}-seg.pt. Sizes: 26n 11.7 MB, 26s 31.1 MB, 26m 70.4 MB, 26l 79.4 MB; 11s 27.8, 11m 60.3, 11l 71.0; v8s 31.1, v8m 65.8, v8l 107.4. For the cubes: set_classes(["red cube", "green cube", "blue cube", "wooden cube"]) or just ["cube"], then geometry from masks.xy as with -seg. The first set_classes() needs (a) the Python package clip from git+https://github.com/ultralytics/CLIP.git (pip-installed at runtime if missing) and (b) the TorchScript text encoder mobileclip2_b.ts, 253.8 MB, downloaded into the current working directory unless it is already there or in weights_dir. YOLOE-11 and YOLOE-v8 use mobileclip_blt.ts, 599.8 MB. Embeddings can be saved once with save_prompt_embeddings("x.npz") and reloaded with load_prompt_embeddings() so later runs need no text encoder.
candidates.fit_for_task: The most practical label-free option in the package, but expect mediocre results. The docs put zero-shot accuracy at 22-40 mAP on LVIS and say a trained closed-set model will beat it. LVIS does have a "cube/square block" category, so a "cube" prompt is plausible. Telling red from green from blue through text is unreliable, so prompt one generic class and classify colour by HSV on the mask. The baskets' coloured floors may fire as false positives: filter by area (about 61x61 px) and by region. Masks cover the whole visible cube, not the top face. Use yoloe-26s-seg.pt, the docs' recommended starting size.
candidates.pip_package: ultralytics==8.4.218 plus clip @ git+https://github.com/ultralytics/CLIP.git (deps: ftfy, regex, tqdm)
candidates.licence: AGPL-3.0 (ultralytics and its CLIP fork); MobileCLIP2 encoder licence not checked
candidates.mps: works for YOLOE-26: PR #27146 reports get_text_pe with mobileclip2_b.ts working on MPS on main. YOLOE-11/v8 text encoding fails on MPS with "Cannot convert a MPS Tensor to float64" (float64 constants inside mobileclip_blt.ts), so for those call set_classes() while the model is still on CPU. Inference itself runs on MPS.
candidates.latency_note: No M-series number published. The prompted head is close to closed-set YOLO speed. My estimate on M4 MPS: 26s-seg about 25-40 ms at imgsz=640 and 70-120 ms at 1280. Not measured. Text encoding is a one-off cost per class list.
candidates.ram_note: Estimate: about 1-1.5 GB while the 254 MB text encoder is loaded; it is rebuilt on each set_classes call and not kept, so steady state is like a normal s model.

from ultralytics.utils.downloads import attempt_download_asset

W = Path("/abs/project/weights")

candidates.family: Ultralytics YOLOE-26 open-vocabulary segmentation, visual prompt
candidates.what: Same *-seg.pt checkpoints as the text mode, but the classes are defined by example boxes on a reference image: visual_prompts={"bboxes": xyxy array, "cls": ids starting at 0}. No text encoder and no clip package are needed. In the lab the user draws one box around a cube (or one per colour) on a reference frame, and the model then finds all similar objects in that frame, in other images, or through a video (the first frame becomes the reference automatically). Passing refer_image sets the classes permanently on the model, so later predict calls need no prompts, and the embeddings can be saved with save_prompt_embeddings.
candidates.fit_for_task: Good fit for a UI: one drawn box, no labels, no 254 MB download. Results come back named object0, object1, ..., so the app must map ids to R/G/B/wood itself. Visual prompts default to conf=0.05. Whether the visual encoder separates same-shaped cubes by colour is unknown and should be tested; the safe design is one generic cube class plus HSV colour. Expect the same whole-cube masks and basket-floor false positives as the text mode.
candidates.weights_id: yoloe-26s-seg.pt (yoloe-26n-seg.pt 11.7 MB as a lighter option)
candidates.mps: unknown for the visual-prompt encoder specifically (no report either way found); the plain inference path works on MPS. The code asserts "Visual prompts need an unfused YOLOE model", and predict() moves and fuses the loaded module in place, so use a fresh YOLOE instance for visual prompting rather than one that already ran text-prompt predictions.
candidates.latency_note: No published M-series number. One extra pass over the reference image when prompts are set, then normal YOLOE speed (my estimate for 26s-seg on M4 MPS: 25-40 ms at 640, 70-120 ms at 1280; not measured).

candidates.what: CNN "segment everything" model: one pass returns class-agnostic masks for every region. Box, point and text prompts then select among those masks (FastSAMPredictor.prompt(everything_results, ...) re-uses one inference). Weights: FastSAM-s.pt 23.9 MB, FastSAM-x.pt 145.0 MB. For the cubes: segment everything, keep masks whose area is near 61x61 px and whose minAreaRect is roughly square, classify colour by HSV inside the mask, and take centre, angle and corners from minAreaRect. Text prompts trigger a 303 MB download (clip_b32_datacomp.ts) and need the clip package; skip them.
candidates.fit_for_task: Reasonable label-free baseline and the only segment-everything model here that is fast enough for video on this Mac. Risks: trained on SA-1B natural images, so cubes that touch each other may merge into one mask, low-contrast plain-wood cubes on white PLA may be missed, and the basket floors become big masks (easy to reject by area). Masks cover the whole visible cube including side faces. Inference only, no training in the package.
candidates.mps: works expected (it is a YOLOv8-seg network on the standard predictor); not specifically reported. The official M4 benchmark ran on CPU.
candidates.latency_note: Official: FastSAM-s 58.0 ms per image on a 2025 M4 Air 16 GB, CPU, PyTorch (ultralytics 8.4.31, torch 2.10.0). On an RTX PRO 6000: 55.9 ms. My estimate at imgsz=1024 with retina masks on MPS: 40-80 ms. Not measured.
candidates.snippet:
from ultralytics import FastSAM
import cv2, numpy as np

model = FastSAM("/abs/project/weights/FastSAM-s.pt")
r = model(frame_bgr, device="mps", imgsz=1024, conf=0.4, iou=0.9, retina_masks=True, verbose=False)[0]  # segment everything
cands = []
for poly in (r.masks.xy if r.masks is not None else []):
    if len(poly) < 3:
        continue
    (cx, cy), (w, h), ang = cv2.minAreaRect(poly.astype(np.float32))
    if 40 <= min(w, h) and max(w, h) <= 90 and min(w, h) / max(w, h) > 0.75:   # about 61 px squares
        cands.append(((cx, cy), ang % 90, cv2.boxPoints(((cx, cy), (w, h), ang))))
# optional prompts on the same model:
# model(frame_bgr, bboxes=[x1, y1, x2, y2]); model(frame_bgr, points=[[x, y]], labels=[1])
# model(frame_bgr, texts="a red cube")   # downloads clip_b32_datacomp.ts (303 MB)

candidates.family: SAM-family wrappers via ultralytics.SAM (MobileSAM, SAM 2 / 2.1, original SAM)
candidates.what: Promptable segmentation: boxes or clicks in, one precise mask per prompt out; with no prompt the wrapper runs "segment everything" over a point grid. Auto-downloaded weights: mobile_sam.pt 40.7 MB; sam2_t/sam2.1_t.pt 78.1; sam2_s/sam2.1_s.pt 92.3; sam2_b/sam2.1_b.pt 161.9; sam2_l/sam2.1_l.pt 449.2; sam_b.pt 375.0; sam_l.pt 1249.5 (sam_h.pt is in the builder map but not in the asset list). The builder is chosen by file name suffix, so do not rename the files. SAM.predict forces imgsz=1024 and retina_masks=True. Uses in the lab: (1) click or box a cube and get an exact mask; (2) refine boxes from a detector or from classic colour thresholding into masks; (3) pre-label training data. SAM2VideoPredictor tracks a prompted object through a video.
candidates.fit_for_task: Useful as an interactive and labelling tool, poor as the runtime pipeline: there are no classes, it needs prompts, and segment-everything is far too slow. If disk allows, ship mobile_sam.pt (41 MB) and sam2.1_t.pt (78 MB). Skip sam_b and sam_l (375 MB and 1.25 GB, slowest). As with the other class-agnostic models, the mask covers the whole visible cube.
candidates.licence: AGPL-3.0 wrapper; upstream weight licences (Meta SAM/SAM 2, MobileSAM) not checked in this run
candidates.mps: unknown: no MPS-specific handling or open MPS bug found for SAM/SAM 2 in the files read, and the official Apple benchmark ran on CPU. Try device="mps" with PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 and fall back to CPU. Predictor code keeps FP16 off on CPU; an FP16 empty-mask bug in MobileSAM was fixed in October 2026.
candidates.latency_note: Official segment-everything on a 2025 M4 Air 16 GB CPU (ultralytics 8.4.31, torch 2.10.0): MobileSAM 23.8 s, SAM2-t 23.4 s, SAM2-b 28.9 s, SAM-b 41.7 s per image. On an RTX PRO 6000: MobileSAM 605 ms, SAM2-t 668 ms, SAM2-b 857 ms, SAM-b 1306 ms. Prompted mode (one encoder pass plus a small decoder) is much cheaper; no M-series figure published, my guess is 0.3-2 s per image.
candidates.ram_note: Estimate: 1-2 GB for MobileSAM and SAM 2.1 tiny/small at 1024 px; several GB for sam_l. Keep only one loaded.

r = model(frame_bgr, bboxes=[[412, 233, 474, 295], [600, 300, 662, 362]], device="mps", verbose=False)[0]  # one mask per box

candidates.what: Separate checkpoints (*-seg-pf.pt) that need no prompt and no text encoder: they label objects from a built-in 4,585-name vocabulary (the RAM++ tag list) and return masks. Sizes: yoloe-26n-seg-pf.pt 16.3 MB, 26s 40.0, 26m 85.6, 26l 94.6, 26x 193.1; yoloe-11s/m/l-seg-pf.pt 27.9/63.6/74.3; yoloe-v8s/m/l-seg-pf.pt 31.3/67.5/110.7. set_classes() on these raises AssertionError. Use in the lab: an exploratory "what does a generic model see on this board" view.
candidates.fit_for_task: Weak. Prompt-free accuracy is the lowest of the three modes (17-31 AP on LVIS), the label a cube receives is unpredictable (block, toy, box, dice, ...), and colour is not part of the output. Only worth its 40 MB as a zero-setup comparison tile; it is not a pipeline candidate.
candidates.mps: works expected (standard predictor path, no text encoder involved); not specifically reported.
candidates.latency_note: The docs measure about +89% forward-pass time at the full 4,585-name vocabulary versus 80 classes (CPU, yoloe-26s-seg.pt). No M-series figure.
candidates.snippet:
from ultralytics import YOLOE

model = YOLOE("/abs/project/weights/yoloe-26s-seg-pf.pt")
r = model.predict(frame_bgr, device="mps", imgsz=1280, conf=0.1, verbose=False)[0]
labels = [r.names[int(c)] for c in r.boxes.cls]   # names from the built-in vocabulary
# nms=False selects the NMS-free head on YOLOE-26 pf checkpoints

candidates.family: Ultralytics YOLO11 / YOLOv8 segmentation and OBB (previous generations)
candidates.what: Same YOLO() API and the same tasks as YOLO26, for comparison or for loading a teammate's older checkpoint. Sizes: yolo11n-seg.pt 6.2 MB, yolo11s-seg.pt 20.7, yolo11m-seg.pt 45.4; yolo11n-obb.pt 5.8, yolo11s-obb.pt 19.9, yolo11m-obb.pt 42.4; yolov8n-seg.pt 7.1, yolov8s-seg.pt 23.9, yolov8m-seg.pt 54.9; yolov8n-obb.pt 6.6, yolov8s-obb.pt 23.3, yolov8m-obb.pt 53.3. Pretraining is COCO for -seg and DOTAv1 for -obb, as for YOLO26.
candidates.fit_for_task: No advantage over YOLO26 for this task (the docs report YOLO26 gains over YOLO11 on seg and OBB, plus an angle loss for square objects). Fine-tuning is needed just the same. The lab's upload path already loads any of these, so do not pre-download them; only fetch one if a side-by-side generation comparison is wanted.
candidates.weights_id: yolo11n-seg.pt, yolo11n-obb.pt, yolov8n-seg.pt, yolov8n-obb.pt (s/m variants exist)
candidates.mps: works with device="mps"; these generations have only the NMS head (nms=False is a no-op).
candidates.latency_note: Official on an M4 Air CPU via ONNX Runtime: YOLO11n-seg 24.3 ms, YOLOv8n-seg 24.8 ms, YOLO26n-seg 25.2 ms per image.

candidates.what: Text-prompted detector with boxes only: no masks, no angle. Weights: yolov8s-worldv2.pt 25.9 MB, yolov8m-worldv2.pt 57.2, yolov8l-worldv2.pt 94.2, yolov8x-worldv2.pt 146.4 (older -world: s 27.2, m 58.6, l 95.7, x 148.0). set_classes() loads OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/32 through the clip package and downloads ViT-B-32.pt, 354 MB, into <weights_dir>/clip. A model with classes set can be stored with model.save("custom.pt") and reloaded without CLIP.
candidates.fit_for_task: Poor fit. Axis-aligned boxes give neither the rotation nor the corners, YOLOE supersedes it (the docs point to YOLOE for masks and visual prompts), and it costs 354 MB of CLIP weights on a nearly full disk.
candidates.mps: unknown for set_classes on MPS (PR #27152 states YOLO-World is not affected by the MobileCLIP float64 problem); inference is a YOLOv8 detector.
candidates.latency_note: No M-series figure; comparable to a YOLOv8 detector of the same size.
candidates.ram_note: Estimate: about 1-1.5 GB while CLIP ViT-B/32 is loaded.
candidates.snippet:
from ultralytics import YOLOWorld

candidates.what: Meta's concept segmentation: a text phrase or exemplar box returns all matching instances with masks. It is supported in ultralytics (SAM3SemanticPredictor for text and exemplars, SAM("sam3.pt") for SAM 2-style points and boxes, video predictors; sam3.1_multiplex.pt for images only). The weights are not auto-downloaded: access must be requested on Hugging Face (facebook/sam3 and facebook/sam3.1 both report gated = manual; an anonymous request for sam3.pt returns HTTP 401) and the file placed by hand. sam3.pt is 3450 MB, sam3.1_multiplex.pt 3503 MB.
candidates.fit_for_task: Not feasible here. No Hugging Face token and a manual approval step four days before the competition; 3.45 GB of weights against 5.7 GB of free disk; 473.6 M parameters on a 16 GB machine; 2.9 s per image even on an RTX PRO 6000. It would probably segment "red cube" well, but it cannot be part of this lab.
candidates.licence: Model card licence field is "other" (Meta's own terms); wrapper AGPL-3.0
candidates.mps: unknown on current versions; MPS fixes for SAM 3 were merged in 8.3.240 (December 2025). Memory is the real blocker on 16 GB.
candidates.latency_note: Official: 2921 ms per image on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (ultralytics 8.4.19, torch 2.9.1). No Apple figure; expect several seconds or worse.
candidates.ram_note: Estimate: more than 7 GB in FP32 (3.45 GB checkpoint, 473.6 M parameters).

packaging: Version: ultralytics==8.4.218, uploaded to PyPI 2026-11-23 (the GitHub release v8.4.218 has the same date). requires-python >=3.8, classifiers 3.8-3.15. Releases land several times a week, so pin the exact version. Do not go below 8.4.111, which carries the MPS box-clamp fix.

Core dependencies (PyPI metadata): numpy>=1.23.0 (on Darwin 2.0.* to 2.3.4 are excluded because of an Accelerate matmul bug, so use numpy>=2.3.5), matplotlib>=3.3.0, opencv-python>=4.7.0,!=4.13.0.90, pillow>=7.1.2, requests>=2.23.0, torch>=1.8.0, torchvision>=0.9.0, psutil>=5.8.0, polars>=0.20.0, nvidia-ml-py>=12.0.0, ultralytics-thop>=2.2.4, and ultralytics-platform>=0.1.102 on Python >=3.11 (pulls httpx).

Current companions on PyPI: torch 2.15.0 (2026-10-28, requires Python >=3.11, macOS arm64 cp312 wheel 138.6 MB), torchvision 0.29.2 (requires torch>=2.14.0, macOS arm64 wheel 1.8 MB), numpy 2.5.5 (requires Python >=3.12), opencv-python 5.1.0.95 (wheel tagged macosx_15_0_arm64, 25.8 MB; fine on macOS 15.7), polars 2.1.0 (polars-runtime-32 wheel 47.6 MB), lap 0.5.14. Python 3.12 satisfies all of them.

Disk estimate, not measured: about 235 MB of wheels to download and roughly 0.8-1.1 GB installed for the ultralytics environment (torch dominates). A sensible weight set (yolo26n/s-seg, yolo26n/s-obb, yoloe-26s-seg, yoloe-26s-seg-pf, FastSAM-s, mobile_sam, sam2.1_t) is 272 MB, or 525 MB with mobileclip2_b.ts.

OpenCV: ultralytics depends on opencv-python (GUI build). The headless variant is a separate distribution, ultralytics-opencv-headless 8.4.218 (same code, depends on opencv-python-headless). Install only one OpenCV flavour (opencv-python, -headless or -contrib) in the environment; on macOS the default opencv-python is fine.

Declare the lazy dependencies yourself so nothing is installed at run time: clip @ git+https://github.com/ultralytics/CLIP.git (needed for YOLOE text prompts, YOLO-World set_classes, FastSAM texts and SAM 3; its deps are ftfy, regex, tqdm, torch, torchvision) and lap>=0.5.12 (needed by model.track). Never install "clip" from PyPI: that name is an unrelated clipboard tool, and the docs warn the wrong clip gives "'SimpleTokenizer' object is not callable".

Runtime auto-install: ultralytics.utils.checks.check_requirements installs missing packages when the module-level flag AUTOINSTALL is true. It uses "uv pip install --no-cache-dir --python <sys.executable> ..." when uv is on PATH, otherwise pip, which would change a uv-managed venv behind the lockfile. Disable it with the environment variable YOLO_AUTOINSTALL=False (also 0/no/off), set before importing ultralytics. Checkpoint loading itself never installs anything.

Settings: stored in settings.json under <YOLO_CONFIG_DIR>/Ultralytics/ when YOLO_CONFIG_DIR is set, otherwise ~/Library/Application Support/Ultralytics/ on macOS. Fonts are cached in the same folder. Keys include weights_dir, datasets_dir, runs_dir, sync, uuid. Defaults are derived from the working directory at first import (weights_dir = "weights", runs_dir = "runs", relative). Set them explicitly: from ultralytics import settings; settings.update({"weights_dir": "/abs/project/weights", "runs_dir": "/abs/project/data/runs", "datasets_dir": "/abs/project/data/datasets", "sync": False}).

Weights location: a bare name such as YOLO("yolo26n-seg.pt") is looked up in the current working directory, then in weights_dir, and otherwise downloaded into the current working directory. Pass an absolute path (YOLO("/abs/project/weights/yolo26n-seg.pt")) and the file is downloaded to exactly that path. Source URL pattern: https://github.com/ultralytics/assets/releases/download/v8.4.0/<name>. The same rule applies to mobileclip2_b.ts (pre-fetch with ultralytics.utils.downloads.attempt_download_asset(Path(weights_dir) / "mobileclip2_b.ts")). YOLO-World's CLIP file goes to <weights_dir>/clip.

Analytics: with settings sync=True (the default) the package sends Google Analytics events on predict/train/val/export (mode, task, model file basename, device, imgsz, per-stage speeds, CPU model, a hashed machine id) and, only for the yolo CLI with sentry-sdk installed, Sentry crash reports. Turn both off with settings.update({"sync": False}) or "yolo settings sync=False"; the value persists in settings.json. The events module is imported when the first predictor is created, so updating right after "import ultralytics" is early enough. YOLO_OFFLINE=1 also disables analytics, the PyPI update check and downloads.

Other environment switches read at import: YOLO_VERBOSE=False quiets logging; ULTRALYTICS_SAFE_LOAD=1 loads .pt files with torch.load(weights_only=True) against an allow-list (needs torch >=2.6). PyTorch side: PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 lets unsupported MPS ops fall back to CPU (ultralytics does not set it); PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO defaults to 1.7, and a lower value such as 1.0 limits MPS allocations on a 16 GB machine.

Side effects of importing ultralytics: it sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 if the variable is unset, calls torch.set_num_threads(min(8, cores-1)) when a cpu/mps device is selected, replaces torch.save with its own wrapper, and creates settings.json. Run inference in a dedicated worker process or thread so these do not surprise the web server.
Licence in one line: ultralytics code and the Ultralytics-trained weights are AGPL-3.0 (an Enterprise licence is the alternative), which is fine for a local, non-distributed student tool.

pitfalls: On a Mac an unset device runs on CPU (the predict docs table says "unset: CUDA GPU, else CPU", and select_device only picks MPS when device is "mps"). Pass device="mps" on every predict call.

Results.speed ({'preprocess','inference','postprocess'} in ms per image) is not synchronised on MPS: Profile only synchronises cuda/npu/xpu, and a PR to add MPS was declined in October 2026. GPU time leaks into whichever stage forces a sync, usually postprocess. Show these numbers as indicative and record your own wall-clock time per image.

YOLO26 has two heads. In 8.4.218 predict and val default to the one-to-many head with NMS; nms=False selects the NMS-free one-to-one head (at most 300 detections, slightly lower accuracy). The old end2end= argument is deprecated and mapped onto nms. Expose it as a toggle and store it with each run.
half= and int8= are deprecated; use quantize=16 for FP16. FP16 is ignored on CPU. FP16 on MPS is untested here, so keep FP32 as the default.

Zero-shot and class-agnostic segmenters (YOLOE, FastSAM, SAM) mask the whole visible cube. With the camera 601 mm up and a 25 mm cube, the side face adds up to about 27 px at the image edge (my geometry estimate from 61 px = 25 mm), which shifts the mask centroid and skews minAreaRect. A fine-tuned model with top-face-only labels avoids this; otherwise correct radially or use the colour of the top face to trim the mask.

The basket floors in mission B are large coloured regions. Reject them by area and squareness (cube top is about 61x61 px) or by restricting detection to the left half; do not rely on a text prompt to separate them.

YOLOE: prompt-free checkpoints (*-seg-pf.pt) reject set_classes(); visual-prompt results are named object0, object1, ... and default to conf=0.05; YOLOE predicts with agnostic_nms=True by default; a freshly loaded *-seg.pt reports 80 numeric placeholder names until prompted.

YOLOE on MPS: for YOLOE-11 and YOLOE-v8, building the text encoder while the model is on MPS raises "Cannot convert a MPS Tensor to float64" (float64 constants in mobileclip_blt.ts; not fixed as of 2026-11-11). YOLOE-26 with mobileclip2_b.ts works. Compute text embeddings on CPU before the first MPS predict and cache them with save_prompt_embeddings().

predict() moves the loaded nn.Module to the device and fuses it in place. Visual prompting asserts an unfused YOLOE model, and whether set_classes() still works after a text-prompted model has been fused on MPS was not checked. Keep one model instance per (weights, prompt mode, class list) and reload from disk when those change.

SAM wrappers pick the architecture from the file name (sam_b.pt, mobile_sam.pt, sam2.1_t.pt, ...; "sam2" or "sam3" in the stem switches predictor), so uploaded or renamed SAM files will fail. SAM.predict always overrides imgsz to 1024 and sets retina_masks=True. Calling it with no prompt runs segment-everything, which took 23-42 s per image on an M4 CPU.

Segmentation masks are low resolution unless retina_masks=True, and at imgsz=640 a 61 px cube is only about 30 px wide in the network input. For corner and angle quality use imgsz=1280 with retina_masks=True, or OBB.

OBB: obb.xywhr is not canonicalised (w may be the short side) and rotation is defined modulo 180 degrees. Take corners from obb.xyxyxyxy and reduce the angle modulo 90 for a square; ultralytics.utils.ops.xyxyxyxy2xywhr gives the canonical long-edge form.

NumPy inputs must be HWC BGR uint8 (the OpenCV convention). Float arrays are cast to uint8, so values must already be 0-255. Frames decoded as RGB (PIL, imageio, browser canvases) need converting, otherwise red and blue swap, which is fatal for a colour task.

Uploaded .pt files are pickles: loading one runs arbitrary code. For a local single-user tool this is acceptable, but set ULTRALYTICS_SAFE_LOAD=1 to restrict loading to known classes. Detect non-Ultralytics files by catching TypeError / ModuleNotFoundError from YOLO(path).

Video: without stream=True all frame results accumulate in RAM. save=True writes annotated output under runs_dir (on macOS an .mp4 with the avc1 fourcc through cv2.VideoWriter) and uses disk on every run. Prefer stream=True plus your own writer or an ffmpeg re-encode (libx264 or h264_videotoolbox with yuv420p and faststart) and a size cap.
model.track() imports lap and auto-installs it if missing; the default tracker config is now tracktrack.yaml. Text prompts import clip the same way, and export installs onnx/coremltools on first use.

Non-ASCII class names (for example Korean labels) switch result.plot() to PIL text and download Arial.Unicode.ttf into the config directory. Keep class names ASCII or draw overlays in the front end from the JSON geometry.

Memory on 16 GB: keep one or two small models loaded and evict the rest (del model; gc.collect(); torch.mps.empty_cache()). Never load sam_l or SAM 3 next to other models. A model instance is not safe to share across threads according to the thread-safety guide; run all inference through one worker queue.

MPS correctness history: predictions on landscape images had x-coordinates clamped to the image height (zero-width boxes) on ultralytics 8.3.199; the fix shipped in 8.4.111 and relies on torch >=2.5. With 8.4.218 and torch 2.15 this should be gone, but a one-off CPU-versus-MPS comparison on a 1280x720 frame is cheap insurance.
Pretrained checkpoints will show nothing useful on the cubes: COCO-80, DOTAv1-15 and Objects365 contain no cube or block class. An empty result from yolo26n-seg.pt is expected, not a bug in the lab.
open_questions: Will labelled frames or a fine-tuned checkpoint exist before 2026-11-29? The two best candidates (yolo26-obb, yolo26-seg) depend on it; without one the lab can only compare YOLOE, FastSAM and classic colour pipelines.
Actual latency of seg/OBB models at imgsz=1280 on this M4 with MPS is unpublished; every 1280 figure above is my estimate. The lab should record wall-clock time per run.
Does YOLOE's visual prompt separate red, green, blue and plain-wood cubes of identical shape, or only find "cube-like" objects? Not documented; needs a test on real frames.

SAM, SAM 2.1 and MobileSAM on MPS: no primary evidence either way, and no prompted-mode latency for Apple Silicon (official figures are CPU segment-everything). FP16 (quantize=16) on MPS is likewise unverified.

Installed size of the Python environment was not measured (about 0.8-1.1 GB estimated) and the disk has roughly 5.7 GB free; check it before adding the 254 MB text encoder or any SAM 2 base/large weights.

Are top faces the only coloured faces? If side faces are also coloured, colour-threshold and whole-cube masks will extend onto the sides away from the image centre, which changes the labelling and post-processing choice.
YOLO27 is announced with seg and OBB variants but unreleased with no date; nothing to plan around for this competition.
